messages:
Jessica M.: FYI, we have a P2 from AcmeCorp — they're seeing repeated billing alerts for their route even though traffic is ~flat since last night. customer says charts show spikes and alerts firing every 5m. attaching screenshots: https://files.internal/acme/billing-spike.png
Tom R.: ack. can you paste the exact alert and time window? also which org/id so we can look at logs?
Jessica M.: org=ACME-ORG (acct 4521). Alert: route_cost_per_min > 0.25 USD for 3/5 windows (5m windows). Happened at 2026-03-16T23:10-23:40 UTC. Query we used in console: `SELECT sum(cost_usd) as c FROM billing.rollups WHERE route_id='acme-pay' AND ts >= '2026-03-16T23:00Z' GROUP BY 5m`
Sanjay (eng-platform): looking. first-pass: not seeing traffic increase in raw ingestion logs for that route. suspicion: partial rollup buckets are being emitted as partials (missing shards) and our aggregator treats missing shards as zeros for the 5m window, which then interacts with the alert math and causes flapping.
Harper (monitoring): we have logs from rollup-workers around that timeframe showing consumer rebalancing + one worker restart. snippet from /var/log/rollup-worker.log: ```
2026-03-16T22:58:12Z INFO kafka consumer rebalance: partitions assigned: [4,5,6]
2026-03-16T22:58:14Z ERROR rollup: shard-7 incomplete, shards_seen=3/4, emitted_partial=true
2026-03-16T22:58:15Z WARN rollup: emitted_partial -> downstream received bucket with missing contributions
```
Jessica M.: that matches customer's screenshot — spikes only show in the 5m chart, hourly looks normal. customer worried about billing accuracy.
Sanjay (eng-platform): quick repro steps I ran locally: 1) produce messages for partition 7, 2) kill worker handling partition 7 mid-window, 3) allow other workers to emit partial bucket. run query: `SELECT count(*) FROM rollups WHERE shard=7 AND ts BETWEEN '2026-03-16T23:05:00' AND '2026-03-16T23:10:00'` returns 0 while others have values.
Sanjay (eng-platform): root cause hypothesis: rollup aggregation currently defaults to "emit_partial=true" on consumer rebalance to reduce latency. that means downstream aggregator receives incomplete buckets and our alerting rule which sums route_cost_per_min treats missing shard contributions as 0, so if a small shard has a negative contribution previously (rounding/adjustment) it can flip thresholds.
Tom R.: can we confirm whether this impacted billing invoices or just dashboard/alerts?
Harper (monitoring): billing pipeline (daily job) consumes raw ingested metrics, not rollups. so invoices unaffected. this is dashboard/alerting only.
Sanjay (eng-platform): mitigation options: 1) short-term: change alert to only fire on >=4/5 non-zero windows (needs config change in console) OR temporarily widen alert window to 15m; 2) rollup immediate fix: set emit_partial=false and backfill missing buckets for the last 2 hours; 3) longer-term: make aggregator treat missing shards as "unknown" and skip alert math if partial.
Tom R.: what commands to backfill? we should offer the customer a remediation path.
Sanjay (eng-platform): run: ```
# manual backfill for route 'acme-pay' for the affected interval
infractl rollup backfill --org ACME-ORG --route acme-pay --from 2026-03-16T22:55:00Z --to 2026-03-16T23:45:00Z
# then verify consumer offsets
kafka-consumer-groups.sh --bootstrap-server kafka:9092 --describe --group rollup-workers
```
Harper (monitoring): I kicked a backfill job for ACME-ORG on staging first to sanity check; backfill completed and dashboard corrected (no spikes). logs show backfill reaggregated missing shard 7 values.
infra-bot: deploy notice: rollup-worker v2.14.1 rolled to canary at 2026-03-17T00:05:00Z
Jessica M.: I'll relay to Acme that invoices are safe, we can offer to run a backfill to fix dashboards and silence alerts. want eng oncall to validate running backfill in prod.
Sanjay (eng-platform): assigning to @oncall-eng to run prod backfill and flip emit_partial=false for 1h. leaving follow-up: create ticket ENG-ROLLUP-312, add monitoring for consecutive partial emits > 1 per hour.
Tom R.: thanks all. Jessica, please do a customer update: we explain cause, mitigation steps, ETA for backfill, and that billing isn't impacted. :thumbsup:
